seoDescription: Learn to build a dynamic, filterable WooCommerce shop page using only Elementor Pro. This guide shows you how to create a custom product grid with the Loop Grid widget and add interactive category and tag filters using the new Taxonomy Filter feature. Enhance your e-commerce site's user experience by creating a clean, minimalistic, and easy-to-navigate product display without extra plugins or custom code, resulting in a more professional and functional online store.

chapters.title: Introduction: Building a WooCommerce Product Filter
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the project: creating a category and tag filter for WooCommerce products using only Elementor Pro features.

chapters.title: Enabling the Taxonomy Filter Feature
chapters.description: Learn how to navigate to Elementor's settings and activate the Taxonomy Filter feature required for the project.

chapters.title: Preparing WooCommerce Products and Categories
chapters.description: This section covers the necessary prerequisite of having products set up in WooCommerce with categories assigned to them.

chapters.title: Creating the Product Archive Template
chapters.description: Follow the steps to create a new Product Archive template from scratch using the Elementor Theme Builder.

chapters.title: Building the Loop Grid Item
chapters.description: This chapter walks through adding a Loop Grid widget and creating a new template for the individual product card.

chapters.title: Connecting Elements to Dynamic WooCommerce Data
chapters.description: Learn how to use dynamic tags to connect the image, title, button, and price widgets to their respective WooCommerce product data.

chapters.title: Styling the Product Card
chapters.description: This chapter details styling the Add to Cart button and setting up the product price element with the correct HTML tag and typography.

chapters.title: Configuring the Loop Grid Widget
chapters.description: Learn to configure the main Loop Grid widget by setting the query to 'Products' and adjusting the number of columns and items per page.

chapters.title: Finalizing Card Layout and Spacing
chapters.description: Adjust the spacing within the product card using gaps for both the main card container and the inner container holding the button and price.

chapters.title: Refining the Grid and Image Size
chapters.description: This part covers advanced loop template options and demonstrates how to adjust the product image height for a better visual layout.

chapters.title: Adding and Positioning the Taxonomy Filter
chapters.description: Discover how to add the Taxonomy Filter widget, place it above the product grid, and link it to the Loop Grid to control the products.

chapters.title: Styling and Configuring the Filter Widget
chapters.description: Explore the various styling and configuration options for the Taxonomy Filter, including direction, alignment, and spacing.

chapters.title: Advanced Filter Settings and Mobile Responsiveness
chapters.description: Learn to manage filter items, customize text, limit the number of categories shown, and enable horizontal scrolling for a better mobile experience.

chapters.title: Styling the 'Pill' Filter Buttons
chapters.description: Follow a step-by-step guide to style the filter buttons into a 'pill' shape, configuring colors and styles for normal, hover, and active states.

chapters.title: Final Results, Alternatives, and Conclusion
chapters.description: Review the completed product filter, discuss its ideal use case, mention advanced alternatives for larger sites, and conclude the tutorial.

summary:
## Core Components
This project uses two key Elementor Pro features to create a filterable product grid for WooCommerce:

*   **Loop Grid Widget**: Used to display a grid of items (in this case, WooCommerce products).
*   **Taxonomy Filter Widget**: A new feature that allows users to filter content based on taxonomies like categories or tags.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Before you start, ensure you have enabled the **Taxonomy Filter** in `Elementor > Settings > Features`.

## Building the Product Card (Loop Item)
1.  **Create Template**: Add the **Loop Grid** widget to your page and click "Create Template" to design the individual product card.
2.  **Add Elements**: Drag in basic widgets for the product's components:
    *   Image
    *   Heading (for Title)
    *   Button (for Add to Cart)
    *   Heading (for Price)
3.  **Use Dynamic Tags**: Connect each widget to the correct WooCommerce data source:
    *   **Image**: Dynamic Tags > Product Image
    *   **Title**: Dynamic Tags > Product Title
    *   **Add to Cart Button**: Link > Dynamic Tags > Add to Cart URL
    *   **Price**: Dynamic Tags > Product Price
4.  **Set Query**: On the main **Loop Grid** widget, change the `Query > Source` from `Posts` to **Products**.

> [!TIP]
> Use an **Inner Container** to place the "Add to Cart" button and the "Price" side-by-side. Set the container's direction to `Row (Horizontal)` and use `Align Items: Center` for vertical alignment.

## Configuring the Filter
1.  **Add Widget**: Drag the **Taxonomy Filter** widget onto the page, placing it *above* the **Loop Grid** widget.
2.  **Link Filter to Grid**: In the filter's settings, select your **Loop Grid** from the `Select a widget` dropdown.
3.  **Choose Taxonomy**: Select the taxonomy you want to filter by, such as **Product Categories** or **Product Tags**.

## Key Styling Tips
*   **Uniform Grid Images**: For the product image in your loop template, set a specific **Height** (e.g., `250px`) and set **Object Fit** to `Cover`. This ensures all product images are the same size, creating a clean grid.

*   **Pill-Style Filters**: To create pill-shaped filter buttons:
    *   Go to the `Style` tab of the **Taxonomy Filter** widget.
    *   Set **Border Radius** to a high value like `50px`.
    *   Use **Padding** to control the shape (e.g., `0.5rem` top/bottom, `1.5rem` left/right).
    *   Customize the `Normal`, `Hover`, and `Active` states with different background and text colors to provide clear visual feedback.

*   **Mobile-Friendly Filters**: Enable the **Horizontal Scroll** option in the filter's `Content > Settings`. This prevents a long list of categories from breaking your layout on mobile devices by making the list horizontally swipable.

> [!NOTE]
> This built-in Elementor filter is ideal for simple, minimalistic shops. For more advanced filtering needs (e.g., multi-select, price sliders), consider dedicated plugins like **Jet Filters** or **WP Grid Builder**.

## Introduction: Building a WooCommerce Product Filter

To get started, there's a couple of things we need to do. First, head over to your Elementor settings, and then from here over to Features. We got to scroll all the way down until you find the taxonomy filter. This is what we're going to be using for our category and tags filter. It works for blog posts, but it also works for products as well. So go ahead and turn that to active.

Now, previously before we had, we would have also had to activate the loop grid, but it's no longer here inside our features. It's already automatically turned on inside Elementor. So let's go ahead and save.

## Preparing WooCommerce Products and Categories

The next thing we got to do is you got to make sure you have your product set up. So, first, add all of your products, or at least add some to get started, and make sure your products all have categories. Once you have all your products added and you got your categories connected to your products, then we're going to go over here to templates and to Theme Builder.
